Where the project stands in the cycle, and what the next step is.

```text
Answers "where am I?" — the question of whoever is picking the work back up.

Unlike doctor (which hunts systemic loose ends in an already assembled project), status
says which PHASE the project is in: is the interview missing? the init? the first
plan? is there work in progress? And, for each state, what the next step is.

It changes nothing.
```

## Usage

```bash
anchors status [flags]
```

## Flags

| Flag | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--root` | `.` | project root |

## Project health — family

Commands of the same family — what tells each apart:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`anchors doctor`](/docs/cli/commands/doctor/) | X-ray of the ecosystem: systemic loose ends, health and maturity |
| [`anchors audit`](/docs/cli/commands/audit/) | Dossier of one file's pending items (gates + doctor), for batch fixing |
| **`anchors status`** | Where the project stands in the cycle, and what the next step is |
| [`anchors task-status`](/docs/cli/commands/task-status/) | The round's report: what is delivered, what remains, and what comes next |
| [`anchors compliance`](/docs/cli/commands/compliance/) | The state of each regulatory duty: how many nodes subject, how many comply |
| [`anchors governs`](/docs/cli/commands/governs/) | Show who each guide governs (and how many) — sizes the audit per guide |
